messages.content:
You are grading an AI assistant's answer to a question about a company handbook.

Question: If I move from GitLab Canada Corp to GitLab LTD (UK), how do the employer contributions differ between the Canadian CPP plan and the UK pension scheme for bonus or commission payments?
Reference answer (written from the handbook): In Canada, GitLab makes employer contributions to the CPP on your behalf, whereas in the UK employer contributions are not applied to bonus or commission earnings.

Passages the assistant was given:
"""
[GitLab Canada Corp > We've Got You Covered > Financial Security & Retirement > Registered Retirement Savings Plan (RRSP) > Important Notes]
- Contribution changes allowed anytime (1-2 payroll cycles to reflect)
- You're responsible for tracking personal RRSP contribution limits
- Bonus and Commission contributions: If you'd like to direct your bonus or commission payments to your RRSP, you can submit a request through [Compass](https://app.serval.com/new-request) before [payroll cutoff](https://internal.gitlab.com/handbook/finance/payroll/?search=payroll). Please note:
  - Ahead of company-wide bonus payouts, Payroll will notify enrolled RRSP team members that a bonus is approaching and will provide a deadline by which requests must be submitted.
  - Bonus and Commission contributions must be made in full — partial contributions are not permitted.
  - Commission contribution elections can only be updated once per quarter.

- Transfers & withdrawals available April 2025

[GitLab LTD (UK) Benefits > We've Got You Covered > Financial Security > Pension Scheme]
If you'd like to direct your bonus or Commission payments to your UK Pension, you can submit a request through [Compass](https://app.serval.com/new-request) before the payroll cutoff. Please note:

- Ahead of company-wide bonus payouts (May and November), you must notify the Payroll team before the [cutoff period](https://internal.gitlab.com/handbook/finance/payroll/) for that month. This request must be submitted for each bonus payout period individually — it cannot be set up as a standing/permanent request.
- Bonus and Commission contributions will be applied as a Salary Sacrifice if you are enrolled in the salary sacrifice feature of the scheme. If you were hired after 13 December 2022, you were automatically enrolled in salary sacrifice. If you are not enrolled under salary sacrifice, contributions will instead be made as relief-at-source contribution.
- Bonus contributions must be made in full — partial contributions are not permitted.
- Employer contributions are not applied to Bonus or Commission earnings.
- Individuals should consider their Annual Allowance (including any carry forward) and any potential tapered Annual Allowance impact. Tracking these amounts is your own responsibility.

Contact Information

- Scottish Widows: 0345 755 6557 | www.scottishwidows.co.uk/gppae
- Willis Towers Watson - Rachel Haggarty: 07385 558317 | rachel.haggarty@wtw.com

[GitLab Canada Corp > We've Got You Covered > Financial Security & Retirement > Registered Retirement Savings Plan (RRSP) > Questions?]
- **Canada Life**: 1-800-724-3402
- **SC Insurance**: info@scinsurance.ca

GitLab makes employer contributions to CPP on your behalf.

---

- **Benefit**: 2x annual earnings (max $500,000)
- **Reductions**: 50% at age 65, terminates at age 71
- **Beneficiaries**: Designate through ManuLife portal using [these instructions](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1P8ekxi7aWF5FxI2wdAkO1dDYSCDEJovm/view?usp=sharing)

[GitLab LTD (UK) Benefits > We've Got You Covered > Financial Security > Pension Scheme]
Salary Sacrifice

Save on National Insurance contributions while building your pension. Team members hired after 13 December 2022 are automatically enrolled. Earlier hires can opt in via [Compass](https://app.serval.com/new-request).

**Salary Sacrifice FAQ**

- Can we change the amount during the period we’re contracted for salary exchange?
  - Yes it is possible to change the amount/increase your employee percent

- What happens if our ‘actual’ salary changes during the period?
  - Your employee contribution is a percent of basic pay so if your basic pay increases the pension contribution will too.

- What happens if we receive a discretionary bonus?
  - Your definition of pensionable pay is basic salary the percent will not automatically be applied to the bonus. Should you wish to contribute part of you bonus to your pension pot you can do that.
- Is it possible to start from any month?
  - Yes it is; it would be processed on the next available payroll.

- My pension statements only show the Employer Contributions. Is it expected?
  - Yes it is; when pension contributions are made via Salary Sacrifice, both Employee and Employer contributions will show as Employer contributions on Scottish Widows statements.

Pension Contribution Percentages

The certification level that has been chosen is basic salary only and will not include commission, bonuses or any over time payments. The contributions will be paid monthly and will be shown on the pay-slips.
"""

Assistant's answer:
"""
For GitLab Canada Corp, the handbook states that GitLab makes employer contributions to CPP on your behalf [3], but it does not specify if these apply to bonus or commission payments. For GitLab LTD (UK), employer contributions are explicitly not applied to Bonus or Commission earnings [2].
"""

First write one sentence of reasoning, then grade three things:
- correctness: "correct" if the answer states the key information in the reference answer without contradicting it (extra correct detail is fine); "partial" if it gets part of it or is vague; "incorrect" if it is wrong, contradicts the reference, or does not answer.
- refused: true if the assistant declined or said it does not know, instead of answering.
- faithful: true if every factual claim in the answer is supported by the passages above (ignore whether it matches the reference). An answer that only refuses counts as faithful.
The grades must agree with your reasoning.
Return JSON with the reasoning first: {"reason": "one sentence", "correctness": "correct" | "partial" | "incorrect", "refused": true/false, "faithful": true/false}
